## In one sentence

Machine learning learns a function from examples so it can make predictions or
represent structure in new data.

## The learning setup

A dataset contains features $X$ and, for supervised learning, a target $Y$. A
model $f_\theta$ maps features to predictions. Training chooses parameters by
minimising a loss on observed examples:

$$
\hat{\theta} = \arg\min_\theta \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n L(y_i, f_\theta(x_i))
$$

The real goal is performance on relevant future data, not memorisation.

## Main learning types

- Supervised learning uses labelled outcomes.
- Unsupervised learning finds structure without a target.
- Reinforcement learning learns through actions and rewards.

Start with a clear prediction target and define what a useful error means.

::: {.callout-important}
A model can be accurate on a test set and still be unsuitable if the test set
leaks information, the deployment population differs, or the metric is wrong.
:::

## Check your understanding

Define features, target, training data, and deployment data for a model that
predicts hospital readmission.
